push_headlines: Europe rallied with US markets shut for Thanksgiving: the STOXX 600 +1.83% to 637.50 and the DAX +2.14% to 25,231.42.
Brazil's Ibovespa +6.07% to 176,799.84, its best day since the election's first round, on reports Luiz Carlos Trabuco may take the Finance Ministry.
Asia bounced back after Wednesday's chip rout: the Nikkei 225 +0.90% to 57,499.16 and the Hang Seng +1.20% to 22,226.88.
on_notice: OPEC+ meets Sunday, November 29 on 2027 output policy, with analysts seeing a market leaning toward surplus and Gulf attack headlines still in play.
The AI trade is still fragile: the Kospi touched +2.60% intraday before ending +0.30%, so watch whether chipmakers hold the rebound into Friday's shortened US session.
Milder-than-feared US tariff proposals fueled the relief rally; reports say they are unlikely to take effect before February or March.

asia.headline: Tokyo and Taipei led a rebound in AI-linked shares; Seoul faded late.
asia.detail: The Nikkei 225 +0.90% to 57,499.16, led by SoftBank and Kioxia. The Kospi +0.30% to 4,711.21 after Wednesday's -6.20% drop, after touching +2.60% intraday. Taiwan's Taiex +2.50%.

china.headline: Hong Kong snapped its losing streak while Shanghai went nowhere.
china.detail: The Hang Seng +1.20% to 22,226.88, back above 22,000 after seven straight declines. The Shanghai Composite was essentially flat at 3,476.88, up less than 0.1%.

europe.headline: European stocks posted a broad relief rally on tariff relief and a tech rebound.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 +1.83% to 637.50, the DAX +2.14% to 25,231.42, the CAC 40 +1.61% to 8,108.74 and the FTSE 100 +1.75% to 10,609.30; Italy's FTSE MIB +2.36% led the majors. Imperial Brands +13.00% on Altria bid talk. The regional tech index is still about -12.00% this month.

latam.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa soared on Finance Ministry hopes and soft inflation.
latam.detail: The Ibovespa +6.07% to 176,799.84, its biggest gain since the first round of the presidential election, as banks led on expectations that Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco will take the Finance Ministry. November's IPCA-15 came in at 0.22%, below October's 0.32%. The commercial dollar -1.26% to R$5.7435, its fourth straight decline.

mideast.headline: Oil held its gains ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, but quotes conflict.
mideast.detail: AP had Brent $90.79 (+0.20%) on Thursday; other reports put it near $91.09 (+0.50%), and one intraday report near $94.97. Supply worries after the attack on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and Strait of Hormuz risk are weighed against a building surplus. No settlement price was found.
